objects.description: Untyped enumeration mapping IANA IP protocol numbers to prefixed constants, with underlying type unsigned int. Mirrors ip_protocol_t values without strong typing.

functions.name: get_ip_protocol_name_by_number_iana
functions.description: Returns the IANA protocol name string for the given 8-bit IP protocol number (e.g., 6 -> "TCP"). Intended for converting wire-level protocol numbers to human-readable names.
requirements: protocol_number must be an unsigned 8-bit value (0–255).
The returned C string must be treated as read-only.
Whether a null pointer can be returned for unknown/unmapped values is unknown (not specified in the header).

functions.name: get_ip_protocol_enum_type_from_integer
functions.description: Converts an 8-bit IP protocol number to the corresponding ip_protocol_t enumeration value. Useful when translating wire values to the strongly-typed enum.
requirements: protocol_as_integer must be an unsigned 8-bit value (0–255).

Mapping behavior for values without a well-known assignment is inferred to return the corresponding UNASSIGNED_XXX/UNKNOWN_XXX/RESERVED enum entries, but exact behavior for unexpected inputs is otherwise unspecified.

functions.name: get_ip_protocol_enum_as_number
functions.description: Converts an ip_protocol_t enumeration value to its numeric protocol number (0–255).
requirements: ip_protocol_enum should be a valid ip_protocol_t enumerator.
Return value is an unsigned 8-bit number (0–255).

functions.name: get_ip_protocol_name
functions.description: Returns the protocol name string for the given ip_protocol_t enum value (e.g., ip_protocol_t::TCP -> "TCP").
requirements: protocol must be a valid ip_protocol_t enumerator.
The returned C string must be treated as read-only.
Whether a null pointer can be returned for enum values without a canonical name is unknown (not specified in the header).

functions.name: read_protocol_from_string
functions.signature: bool read_protocol_from_string(const std::string& protocol_string, ip_protocol_t& ip_protocol_enum);
functions.description: Parses a protocol name string and, on success, writes the corresponding ip_protocol_t value to the output parameter. Returns true on successful parsing, false otherwise.
requirements: protocol_string should contain a recognizable protocol name (exact accepted formats/case/aliases are unknown from the header).
ip_protocol_enum must be a valid, writable reference; its value is only meaningful if the function returns true.
Callers must check the boolean return value before using ip_protocol_enum.

data_types.description: A human-readable Internet protocol identifier as text. Examples include names like "TCP", "UDP", "ICMP", "IGMP", or other IANA protocol names. Case sensitivity and accepted aliases may vary by implementation; input is free-form text that the parser attempts to map to a known IP protocol.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces protocol name strings as bytes for read_protocol_from_string()
# It focuses on valid IANA protocol names, common aliases, case variations, spacing,
# numeric forms, and prefixed names to exercise different parsing branches while
# remaining mostly valid/meaningful inputs.

_VALID_PRIMARY = [
    # Common well-known protocols likely supported
    "TCP", "UDP", "ICMP", "IGMP", "IPV4", "IPV6", "SCTP", "DCCP", "GRE", "ESP", "AH",
    "RSVP", "EIGRP", "OSPFIGP", "L2TP", "PIM", "VRRP", "UDPLITE", "IPCOMP", "ROHC",
    # A few less common but present in the enum
    "HOPOPT", "IPV6_ROUTE", "IPV6_FRAG", "IPV6_ICMP", "IPV6_NONXT", "IPV6_OPTS",
    "IPIP", "ENCAP", "ETHERIP", "MPLS_IN_IP", "PGM", "RSVP_E2E_IGNORE",
]

# Plausible aliases/variants that implementations often accept
_ALIASES = [
    "ip",              # generic/ambiguous
    "icmpv6",          # alias of IPV6-ICMP
    "icmp6",           # another common alias
    "ip6",             # alias for IPv6
    "ip4",             # alias for IPv4
    "igp",             # lower-case common
    "ipv6-icmp",       # dashed form
    "ipv6_route",      # underscore form
    "no next header",  # textual description for NONXT
    "hopopt",          # lower-case
    "rsvp-e2e-ignore", # dashed
    "ah", "esp", "gre", "sctp", "dccp", "udp", "tcp",
]

# Numeric forms as strings (decimal) covering interesting edges and known values
_NUMERIC_STRINGS = [
    "0",   # HOPOPT
    "1",   # ICMP
    "6",   # TCP
    "17",  # UDP
    "41",  # IPV6
    "58",  # IPV6-ICMP
    "132", # SCTP
    "136", # UDPLITE
    "255", # RESERVED
]

# Decorators/format permutations to test case-insensitivity and trimming
def case_permutations(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    modes = [
        str.upper,
        str.lower,
        str.title,
        lambda x: ''.join((c.upper() if i % 2 == 0 else c.lower()) for i, c in enumerate(x)),
        lambda x: x,  # unchanged
    ]
    return rnd.choice(modes)(s)

def add_whitespace(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Add varying leading/trailing whitespace including tabs and spaces
    lead = ''
    tail = ''
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        lead = ' ' * rnd.randint(0, 3) + ('\t' if rnd.random() < 0.3 else '')
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        tail = ('\t' if rnd.random() < 0.3 else '') + ' ' * rnd.randint(0, 3)
    return lead + s + tail

def with_prefix_suffix(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Try common textual prefixes or separators that parsers may accept
    options: List[str] = [
        s,
        f"proto {s}",
        f"protocol {s}",
        f"{s} protocol",
        f"next header {s}",
        f"{s}".replace('_', '-'),
        f"{s}".replace('-', '_'),
    ]
    return rnd.choice(options)

def maybe_comment(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally append an inline comment-like suffix
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        suffixes = [" # comment", " // note", " ; remark"]
        s += rnd.choice(suffixes)
    return s

def build_candidate(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    choice_bucket = rnd.random()
    if choice_bucket < 0.45:
        base = rnd.choice(_VALID_PRIMARY)
    elif choice_bucket < 0.65:
        base = rnd.choice(_ALIASES)
    elif choice_bucket < 0.85:
        base = rnd.choice(_NUMERIC_STRINGS)
    else:
        # Construct from enum-looking names, including UNKNOWN/UNASSIGNED which may still be parsable
        prefixes = ["UNASSIGNED", "UNKNOWN", "MOBILITYHEADER", "IPV6_OPTS", "IPV6_NONXT"]
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            base = rnd.choice(prefixes)
            if base in ("UNASSIGNED", "UNKNOWN"):
                base = f"{base}_{rnd.randint(99, 230)}"  # stay in defined ranges
        else:
            base = rnd.choice(_VALID_PRIMARY)
    s = base
    s = case_permutations(s, rnd)
    s = with_prefix_suffix(s, rnd)
    s = add_whitespace(s, rnd)
    s = maybe_comment(s, rnd)
    # Keep within 4096 bytes trivially; these are short strings.
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    s = build_candidate(rnd)
    # Return as bytes UTF-8
    return s.encode('utf-8')
